title: Shardmap TTL drift caused split-shard serving and deferred rollback quarantine
creator: Ava Morales
description: During a staged rollout of a sharded LLM variant (split-shard placement for multi-GPU serving), a TTL misconfiguration in the shardmap propagation layer allowed an older shardmap to persist on a subset of frontends. That resulted in a minority of requests being routed to a mixed set of backends: some frontends served with the new shard placement while others continued using the old mapping. The mismatch caused inconsistent KV cache lookups, increased p95 latency by ~210ms for affected requests, and a surge in error rates for session-affinity flows. An automated rollback was attempted but could not complete because the model version pin for the canary was left in a quarantined state by a prior orchestration failure, so rollback was deferred and manual intervention was required.
timeline: 2026-03-01T09:12Z - Canary rollout of shard-placement v3 started (canary weight 5%).
2026-03-01T09:28Z - On-call alerted: p95 generation latency increased for route /chat/session in region us-east-1.
2026-03-01T09:33Z - Error spike: KV cache misses and session affinity errors observed; affected requests ~4.7% of total traffic to route.
2026-03-01T09:40Z - Initial mitigation: reduce canary weight to 0% and attempt automated rollback (orchestrator returned 'pin_quarantined').
2026-03-01T09:45Z - Rollback failed due to version-pin lock held by failed promotion job; orchestrator returned inconsistent state across leaders.
2026-03-01T10:05Z - Manual operator intervention: clear stale pin, force-deactivate canary in region, and reconcile shardmap TTL via control-plane broadcast.
2026-03-01T10:17Z - Traffic normalized; latency and error rates returned to baseline by 10:25Z.
2026-03-02 - Incident declared and pagerduty postmortem initiated; evidence archived to Drive and PRs opened for fixes.
detection_summary: Alerting triggered by Console SLO monitors on /chat/session p95 and by a spike in KV cache miss rate. On-call correlation with recent rollout window pointed to shardmap change. The regression was reproducible in canary region when a TTL mismatch was injected in staging.
root_cause: Shardmap propagation code relied on a per-leader TTL refresh that was incorrectly set to 0s under a new config flag. As a result, some frontends never refreshed to the new shardmap and continued serving old placement. The orchestrator's rollback path depends on unpinning the version; a prior transient promotion failure left the version in a quarantined 'pin' state and the automated rollback path did not handle quarantined pins correctly, causing the rollback to abort rather than fail open.
mitigation_summary: Immediate: scale canary weight to 0 and manual unpin+deactivate steps by SREs. Reconciled shardmap by forcing propagation broadcast and restarting affected frontend nodes to pick up fresh shardmap. Added a temporary guard in orchestrator to allow rollback when pin state is quarantined with operator confirmation.
postmortem_summary: This incident combined a configuration regression (shardmap TTL) with an edge-case in rollback semantics (quarantined pins). The combination allowed a small percentage of traffic to experience mixed-shard routing, leading to cache inconsistencies and latency regressions. No customer data was exposed; impact was service degradation for a subset of sessions. Action items focus on fixing TTL defaults, hardening rollback semantics, improving rollout preflight checks, and adding targeted observability for shardmap staleness.

runbook_changes: Add explicit step to detect shardmap TTL=0 misconfig and fail preflight.
Add operator-confirmed unpin procedure with audit trail and rollback gating in console.
Document forced-reconciliation (broadcast + controlled frontend restart) as a remediation step.
qa_criteria: Shardmap TTL default enforced by config unit tests and e2e test covering leader rotation.
Orchestrator rollback path exercises quarantined-pin-approval and logs audit entries.
New shardmap-staleness alert fires in staging when we induce TTL drift.
notes: Operator unpin endpoint currently requires 2 approvals; we added temporary bypass for incident recovery but will not make it permanent.
Consider follow-up to make shardmap propagation use push+confirm rather than eventual TTL-only refresh for critical routes.
Investigate whether kv-cache keys should include shardmap_version as part of the cache key to avoid cross-version pollution.
